references.text: The first servant reported that his mina had earned ten minas and was given authority over ten cities. The second servant in verse 18 follows the same pattern, but with five minas and five cities, showing a proportional reward for faithfulness. See [ref:Luk 19:16-17|Luke 19:16-17].
The contrast between the faithful servant in verse 18 and the unfaithful servant who hid his mina underscores the principle: "He who has, will be given more" ([ref:Luk 19:24-26|Luke 19:24-26]).

In Jesus' parable of the talents in Matthew, the second servant received two talents and earned two more – parallel to the second servant in Luke who earned five minas. Both receive praise and reward. See [ref:Matt 25:22-23|Matthew 25:22-23].

Paul teaches that "each will receive their own wages according to their own work." This principle of proportional reward based on faithfulness is reflected in the parable where the second servant is given responsibility over five cities for his five minas. See [ref:1 Kor 3:8|1 Corinthians 3:8].

The principle that whoever is faithful in little is also faithful in much underlies why the second servant is rewarded with authority over five cities for faithfully managing one mina. See [ref:Luk 16:10|Luke 16:10].
The parable of the talents in [ref:Matt 25:14-15|Matthew 25:14-15] is a parallel to the entire parable of the minas, where a master entrusts his servants with money to manage while he is away.
